title: 第7章 历史第8章 任务第9章 收藏
slug: 诡秘星轨交织的夜第222章
content_zh:
乘坐普嘉特安排的马车，他们很快到达了水仙花街。
这是一条绿树成荫的街道，两旁是整齐的住宅，每栋房子前都有个小花园，间隔着铸铁栏杆。
七号的门牌挂在围栏上，白色油漆在阳光下微微发亮。
“就是这里了。”普嘉特取出钥匙打开前门。
前院不大，但打理得很好，一条石板小径通向深蓝色的正门。
进门后是宽敞的门厅，左边是客厅，右边是餐厅，后面是独立的厨房和一间小佣人房。
“一层布局很实用，”普嘉特介绍道，“厨房有独立的食品储藏室，里面厨具都能正常使用。”
大部分窗户都是朝阳，采光良好，加上公司有派人打扫屋子，一眼望去，还不错。
二楼有两间次卧和一间客卧，每间都有足够的衣柜空间和一个小梳妆台。
三楼是主卧套房，包括卧室、书房和一个让莫甘娜特别感兴趣的收藏室。
后花园比莫甘娜预期的更大，种着几株玫瑰和常绿灌木，还有一个石制小喷泉。
花园尽头有个后门，通向一条外面。
当下，莫甘娜就决定定下这套房屋。
“我就要这套了。租金一周一镑，家具使用费五苏勒，押金五镑，对吗？”
“是的小姐，”普嘉特先生显然做好了准备，在准备签字的时候就拿出了合同，这都是随身携带的，主打一个随时随地，“如果小姐您确定了的话就签下合同，事务所提供免费的搬运服务，需要我们将小姐您的行李送过来吗？”
“体贴的服务，”莫甘娜先是在合同上签下了自己的名字，然后从手提包中取出一打钞票，“如果我没有算错的话，一年的租金，加上事务所的收费，应该是七十镑。”
普嘉特略显惊讶于莫甘娜的爽快和现金支付能力，但职业素养让他很快恢复常态，“是的，小姐，您的智慧与慷慨让我佩服。”
几分钟后，普嘉特拿着巨款、租赁合同以及莫甘娜刚刚给予的旅馆地址离开了水仙花街七号，屋子里，只剩下了莫甘娜一个人。
重新逛了一下房子，粗略看了看需要购买的东西，莫甘娜就在书房用仅剩的几张纸和笔开始写信。
一封是因为倒吊人先生的，幸好维斯珀家族在普利兹港也有一些人脉，这件事情，只需要莫甘娜一封信就可以完成。

而另外一封则是要寄到黑荆棘安保公司，告知邓恩队长自己现在的地址的。
眨眼又到中午了，两位厨师也到达水仙花街七号。
一位是四十岁左右，名叫托马斯·马丁的中年男子，手指粗壮但干净，看起来是专业的厨师，只是不知道因为什么原因从餐厅离职了，只能选择成为并不算稳定的家庭厨师。
另外一位是叫玛丽·基尔的女士，三十上下，看着是很普通的家庭妇女。
莫甘娜在尝试过两位的餐食之后选择了玛丽女士，因为，这位女士的家庭菜比较符合莫甘娜的口味，她不像贝克兰德的那些某些贵族，追求的都是什么某某某餐厅的招牌菜，主打一个高贵好看，但是味道不咋地。
所以，莫甘娜拒绝了托马斯先生的求职，并快速与玛丽女士签下了合同。
content_en:
Taking the carriage arranged by Pugat, they quickly arrived at Daffodil Street.
This is a tree-lined street lined with neat houses, each with a small garden in front of it and separated by cast iron railings.
The door number of No. 7 hangs on the fence, and the white paint shines slightly in the sun.
"This is it." Pougat took out the key and opened the front door.
The front yard is small but well-kept, and a stone path leads to the dark blue main entrance.
After entering, there is a spacious foyer, with the living room on the left, the dining room on the right, and an independent kitchen and a small maid's room at the back.
"The layout on the first floor is very practical," Pugat said. "The kitchen has a separate pantry, and the kitchen utensils can be used normally."
Most of the windows are facing the sun and the lighting is good. In addition, the company has sent people to clean the house. At first glance, it looks good.
There are two secondary bedrooms and a guest bedroom on the second floor, each with ample closet space and a small dresser.
The third floor is the master suite, which includes a bedroom, a study, and a collection room that is of particular interest to Morgana.
The back garden was larger than Morgana expected, with several roses and evergreen shrubs and a small stone fountain.
There is a back door at the end of the garden, which leads outside.
At that moment, Morgana decided to book this house.
"I want this apartment. The rent is one pound a week, the furniture is five soles, and the deposit is five pounds, right?"
"Yes, Miss," Mr. Pudgart was clearly prepared. He took out the contract when he was about to sign. He carried it with him everywhere, "If you are sure about it, sign the contract. The office provides free moving services. Do you want us to send your luggage here, Miss?"
"Considerate service," Morgana signed her name on the contract first, and then took out a dozen bills from her handbag. "If I'm not mistaken, one year's rent, plus the firm's fees, should be seventy pounds."
Pudgart was slightly surprised by Morgana's willingness and ability to pay cash, but his professionalism quickly returned him to normal, "Yes, Miss, I admire your wisdom and generosity."
A few minutes later, Pudgart left No. 7 Daffodil Street with a huge sum of money, a lease contract, and the hotel address Morgana had just given. Morgana was the only one left in the house.
After browsing the house again and briefly looking at the things she needed to buy, Morgana started writing a letter in the study with the few remaining pieces of paper and pen.
One letter was for Mr. Hanged Man. Fortunately, the Vesper family also had some connections in Pulitzer Harbor. This matter only needed a letter from Morgana to complete.
The other letter was to be sent to the Blackthorn Security Company to inform Captain Dunn of his current address.
In the blink of an eye, it was noon again, and the two chefs also arrived at No. 7 Daffodil Street.
One was a middle-aged man named Thomas Martin, who was about forty years old. He had thick but clean fingers. He seemed to be a professional chef. He just left the restaurant for unknown reasons and could only choose to become a home cook, which was not stable.
The other one is a lady named Mary Keel, who is around thirty and looks like a very ordinary housewife.
Morgana chose Ms. Mary after trying both of their meals, because this woman's family dishes were more in line with Morgana's taste. She was not like some of the nobles in Backlund who pursued the signature dishes of a certain restaurant, which were noble and beautiful, but the taste was not good.
Therefore, Morgana rejected Mr. Thomas's job search and quickly signed a contract with Ms. Mary.
